name: New Incentives (Founders Pledge)
summary: Cash incentives for routine childhood vaccination in northern Nigeria. Founders Pledge's recommendation page states only a multiple of cash transfers, more than 10, which this model takes at face value and turns into healthy years through the site's shared value of a dollar given as cash.

source.title: New Incentives (charity recommendation)

sections.title: Founders Pledge's figure
sections.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figures, as its recommendation page states them. It publishes no spreadsheet for this recommendation, so these are the model's only evaluator rows.

sections.title: From a multiple of cash to units of value
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: Founders Pledge states its result as a multiple of cash transfers. The site values cash at one shared benchmark (GiveWell's 0.00335 units of value per dollar), so the multiple times that benchmark is units of value (doubled income-years) per dollar.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness, multiple of direct cash transfers

source.title: Founders Pledge, New Incentives (recommendation page)
source.quote: We estimate that New Incentives is more than 10 times as effective as direct cash transfers.

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's figure, quoted on its page: "more than 10 times as effective as direct cash transfers". The page says it rests on GiveWell's cost-effectiveness analysis; Founders Pledge publishes no sheet of its own. We take 10, the floor the page states, so the result is if anything low. GiveWell's own New Incentives models are on the site separately.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. Founders Pledge states the result as a multiple of cash transfers; read against its own GiveDirectly benchmark of 2022 ($164 per WELLBY-equivalent, and 1.898 WELLBY-equivalents per doubled income-year), 10 times cash is 0.0321 units of value (doubled income-years) per dollar. The site turns every multiple of cash into units of value with one shared benchmark, GiveWell's 0.00335 units of value per dollar given as cash, so that "10 times cash" means the same in every model; Founders Pledge's own benchmark comes to almost the same (0.0032). GiveWell's November 2024 estimate for GiveDirectly in Kenya is 2.6 times higher; it sets the top of the benchmark's range. Because 10 is the floor the page states, the result is a lower bound. Because it goes through a multiple, the site's value-of-life setting has no effect here. The evaluator view uses Founders Pledge's 0.0321, at its own rate of 1.95 doubled income-years per healthy year (3.7 / 1.898).

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Much of New Incentives' spending is the cash incentives themselves, so staff are a smaller share than in programs where staff deliver the help. Our judgment; we haven't seen its breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: Healthy years per dollar. With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
